title: Electronics & Measurements
summary: Semiconductor basics, diodes/Zener, BJT relations, op-amp gains, number systems and gates, instruments and bridges, meter range extension.
definitions: Doped with pentavalent donors (P, As, Sb); majority carriers electrons.
Doped with trivalent acceptors (B, Ga, In, Al); majority carriers holes.
Operated in reverse breakdown as a voltage regulator.
Inverting input held ≈ 0 V by feedback in an inverting amplifier.
NAND and NOR — any logic function can be built from either alone.
Measures insulation resistance with high DC test voltage.
Slow rotation of energy-meter disc at no load; stopped by holes in the disc.
facts: Barrier potential: Si 0.7 V, Ge 0.3 V.
Zener breakdown (heavy doping) < ~5 V; avalanche > ~6 V.
CE: voltage and current gain, 180° phase shift. CC (emitter follower): A_v ≈ 1, buffer. CB: low input impedance.
FET: voltage-controlled, very high input impedance, unipolar.
Ideal op-amp: infinite gain and Z_in, zero Z_out, infinite bandwidth.
PMMC: DC only, uniform scale. Moving iron: AC and DC, square-law scale. Induction energy meter: AC only. Electrodynamometer: wattmeter.
Bridges: Wheatstone (medium R), Kelvin double (low R < 1 Ω), Maxwell (medium-Q L), Hay (high-Q L), Schering (C and tan δ), Wien (frequency), Anderson (L).
Ammeter: series, very low resistance. Voltmeter: parallel, very high resistance.
Clamp meter measures current without breaking the circuit. Lissajous patterns give frequency ratio and phase.
traps: Inverting gain is negative; non-inverting has the extra +1.
Kelvin double bridge is for LOW resistance; megger is for HIGH (insulation) resistance.

examples.q: Convert a 1 mA, 100 Ω movement to (a) 1 A ammeter, (b) 100 V voltmeter.
Zener regulator: V_in 20 V, V_Z 12 V, R_S 200 Ω, R_L 1 kΩ. Zener current?
